title: Use comparison cards when two teaching choices must answer the same learner need side by side.
summary: The comparison stays useful because each row asks one decision question before either choice is described.
footer: When one option clearly fits every row, use a short step sequence instead.

callout.label: Selection rule
callout.value: Compare only choices that share the same decision points.

criteria.label: Learner has not seen the target action before
criteria.leftValue: Show one complete example so the expected move is visible.
criteria.rightValue: Use only after the learner has a clear reference to recall.

criteria.label: Learner can already begin but needs a small reminder
criteria.leftValue: A full model may take over an action the learner can start alone.
criteria.rightValue: Ask one focused question that directs attention back to the next move.

criteria.label: Adult needs to notice where the routine breaks down
criteria.leftValue: The model makes the intended sequence explicit for later comparison.
criteria.rightValue: The prompt reveals which step the learner can retrieve independently.

criteria.label: Time is short and the next action must stay visible
criteria.leftValue: Use the shortest possible demonstration with no extra explanation.
criteria.rightValue: Use one cue when the learner already knows the routine.
